summary.name: IP PBX
summary.one_liner: An IP PBX is a software-based telephony system that uses Internet Protocol to carry voice, data and video over packet-switched networks.
use_cases: Running an office phone system on a server
Setting up inbound and outbound call center operations
Replacing traditional PBX hardware with software
Connecting business calls to PSTN via SIP trunks
Adding IVR, conference calling and text-to-speech to telephony
summary.what_it_does: The page describes IP PBX as telephony software hosted on a standard desktop or server, with capacity scaled to expected traffic and criticality. It explains that IP PBX uses packet-switched networks so voice, data and video share the same infrastructure, unlike circuit-switched traditional PBXs. Features mentioned include conference calling, XML-RPC control of live calls, IVR, TTS/ASR, PSTN interconnection for analog and digital circuits, and protocols such as SIP, Inter-Asterisk eXchange, H.323 and Jingle. It lists 3CX Phone System and Asterisk as IP PBX software, and names several Asterisk-derived systems including Bicom Systems, Dialexia, trixbox and FreeSWITCH.
notable: Software-based PBX running on ordinary desktops or servers
Asterisk is named as the Linux-based product with the largest market share
Supports SIP, H.323, Inter-Asterisk eXchange and Jingle protocols
Many IP PBX products are derived from Asterisk
caveats: Article is general overview and is flagged as having multiple issues
Page does not state pricing or licensing for the listed products
